links.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs with knowledge-graph RAG versus No-RAG across graph sources, probes and temperatures
links.effect: Scope-matched retrieval (notably G2) gave the most consistent gains; indiscriminate graph unions often reduced accuracy; larger models matched or exceeded KG-RAG with No-RAG on Probe 1.
links.quote: Results show that scope alignment between probe and KG is decisive: precise, scope-matched retrieval (notably $\mathbb{G}_2$) yields the most consistent gains, whereas indiscriminate graph unions often introduce distractors that reduce accuracy.

unlisted_practices: Precision-first, scope-matched knowledge-graph selection over breadth-first unions for RAG
Matching model size to retrieval need (smaller models benefit more from well-scoped retrieval)

screen.practice: retrieval grounding with scope-matched knowledge graphs
screen.reason: The study tests whether adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with specific domain knowledge graphs improves factual accuracy and reasoning compared to baseline (No-RAG) LLMs across multiple models and decoding temperatures.

primary.practice: retrieval grounding via domain knowledge graphs
